title: Ring signatures for code
description: Ring signatures prove 'one of these N people signed this' without revealing which. Applied to code commits, a developer proves membership in the authorized group — the commit is legitimate — while staying anonymous within it. Rivest-Shamir-Tauman's construction, now protecting commit attribution.
method: Sign with the ring of group public keys; the verifier checks group membership; the signer stays hidden among the ring.
usage: Use for anonymous-but-authorized contributions; size the ring for your anonymity set.

demo.code:
print('commit signed with ring of 50 maintainers')
print('verified: signed by A maintainer (which one: hidden)')

title: Blind-signature code review
description: Blind signatures let a reviewer approve code without seeing whose it is: the author blinds the commit, the reviewer signs the blinded version, the author unblinds. Reviews stay merit-based — no favoritism, no bias against newcomers — while approvals remain verifiable.
method: Blind the commit; reviewer signs blinded; unblind to a valid signature on the real commit; bias eliminated structurally.
usage: Use for promotion-sensitive reviews; the process must genuinely hide identity (no side channels).

demo.code:
print('commit blinded -> reviewer approves quality -> unblinded signature valid')
print('reviewer never knew the author: no bias possible')

title: Deniable commit encryption
description: Deniable encryption lets an author plausibly claim a commit decrypts to innocuous content: two keys, two plaintexts, and no way to prove which is real. Under coercion, the author surrenders the decoy key — the real contribution stays hidden and deniable.
method: Encrypt with deniable scheme; decoy key reveals innocuous content; coercion yields the decoy; the real content is unprovable.
usage: Reserve for high-risk environments; deniability must be technically sound, not just claimed.

demo.code:
print('commit decrypts with decoy key -> "typo fixes"')
print('real key -> the actual patch (unprovable under coercion)')

title: Mixnet commit submission
description: Commits submitted through a mixnet (Tor, Nym) hide the network origin: timing and routing decorrelate the submission from the submitter. Combined with anonymous credentials, the commit's network trail goes cold — attribution-resistant at the transport layer.
method: Submit via mixnet; batch and delay to defeat timing analysis; the repository sees the commit, not the source IP.
usage: Use for sensitive submissions; understand mixnets don't hide content fingerprints (style, timing of work).

demo.code:
print('commit pushed via Tor (3 hops, batched)')
print('repository: commit received; source IP: unknown')

title: Attribution watermarking (for leaks)
description: The flip side: invisible per-recipient watermarks in distributed code so leaks can be attributed. Each recipient's copy differs subtly (whitespace, equivalent instruction choices); a leaked copy identifies its source. Anonymity for contributors, accountability for distributors.
method: Vary the build per recipient invisibly; record the mapping securely; leaked code reveals its recipient.
usage: Use for sensitive pre-release distribution; protect the watermark mapping fiercely.

demo.code:
print('build for partner P3: instruction-choice fingerprint f9a1')
print('leaked binary: fingerprint f9a1 -> source: P3')

title: Anonymous reputation systems
description: Reputation without identity: anonymous credentials let contributors prove 'I have 100 merged PRs' without revealing which account earned them. Trust transfers across pseudonyms and contexts — the work vouches for the worker, whoever they are.
method: Issue credentials for achievements; prove credential possession anonymously; reputation composes across contexts.
usage: Design credential issuance carefully (who attests achievements); prevent double-spend of reputation.

demo.code:
print('ZK proof: "I hold 100-PR credential from project X"')
print('new project: trusted contributor (identity still hidden)')

title: Zero-knowledge authorship proofs
description: Prove 'I wrote this' (or 'an authorized author wrote this') in zero knowledge: the prover demonstrates knowledge of the signing key or membership credential without revealing which. Authorship claims become verifiable and private simultaneously.
method: ZK proof of key knowledge or group membership; the verifier learns the claim's truth, not the author's identity.
usage: Use where authorship must be proven but identity must stay hidden (bounties, disclosures).

demo.code:
print('ZK proof: "I hold the key that signed release v2.3"')
print('verified: true (which key: hidden)')

title: Anonymous whistleblowing channels
description: SecureDrop-style channels let insiders leak code or documents proving wrongdoing without revealing themselves: Tor hidden services, air-gapped submission, stripped metadata. The channel's security properties — not promises — protect the source.
method: Tor-based submission; metadata stripped; air-gapped review; the source's identity never touches the system.
usage: Operate the channel with real operational security; test it; protect sources absolutely.

demo.code:
print('submission via Tor: documents + code, metadata stripped')
print('newsroom reviews air-gapped; source: unidentifiable by design')
